newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle seen steady - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle seen steady - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets next week were seen steady at $66.00 per cwt following this week's active sales, feedlot sources said.
Sales were up $1.00 from a week ago amid strong packer demand for cattle to meet firm beef interest.

Prices also were supported by the first major storm and cold blast of the season over the past two weeks in Kansas, the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma Panhandle, which set cattle back nearly 20 to 25 pounds in gains.
With the lower weights, packers will need to buy more cattle to produce the same amount of beef, the sources said.
Cattle weights have been running well behind last year anyway because strong packer demand spurred early marketings at the feedlots, they said.
Average cattle weights the week ended Saturday were estimated at 1,154 lbs, compared with 1,162 last week and the actual average of 1,193 last year, USDA said.
Beef demand was strong this week as retailers stock up for immediate needs, according to USDA in its national carlot beef trade weekly review.
Lightweight choice cuts were up $1.30 per cwt at $102.02 for the week on Thursday, USDA said.
